name: Husqvarna Sport Glasses
title: Husqvarna Sport Glasses for Saw and Brush Work
meta: Husqvarna Sport Glasses are light wraparound safety glasses for running a saw, chipping and hauling brush. Fit, lens care and what to expect for the money.
tagline: Light wraparound safety glasses for saw work, chipping and cleanup.
summary: Husqvarna Sport Glasses are a lightweight, wraparound pair of safety glasses meant for everyday saw and ground work. They are the kind of glasses you keep on all day while bucking, feeding the chipper and raking up, and cheap enough to keep a spare pair in the truck.
highlights: Wraparound frame for side coverage
Light enough to wear all day
Sporty fit that stays put when you bend and lift
Works under most helmets and with ear muffs
Low cost, easy to keep spares
specs: Chainsaw, chipper and general ground work

body.h: Where these glasses earn their keep
p: Most eye injuries on a tree crew do not come from the saw itself. They come from chips kicked off the chain, twigs snapping back while you drag brush, and dust blowing out of the chipper chute. A pair of wraparound glasses that you actually leave on is the fix, and that is what the Husqvarna Sport Glasses are built for.

The wraparound shape covers the sides of your eyes, where a mesh visor alone can let fine sawdust in. Many climbers and saw operators wear glasses under a mesh visor for that reason, especially when cutting dry or dead wood. Browse the rest of our eye protection if you want tinted lenses or a helmet visor to pair them with.

Check that the arms clear your ear muff cushions without breaking the seal; thin temples matter if you wear helmet-mounted muffs all day. Clean the lenses with water and a soft cloth rather than a sleeve full of sawdust, which scratches them fast.

Replace glasses when the lens is pitted, scratched in your line of sight, or the frame is cracked. Confirm the marking on the lens and frame meets the eye protection standard your employer or the job requires before relying on them.
Keep a second pair in the truck. Glasses get sat on, scratched and lost in the brush pile, and a groundie who has to finish the day without them is the one who ends up with a chip in the eye.

faq.q: Can I wear these under a mesh visor?
faq.a: Yes. Glasses under a mesh visor is a common setup because the visor stops larger debris and the glasses catch the fine dust that gets through the mesh.

faq.q: Are these safety rated?
faq.a: Check the markings on the lens and frame of the pair you buy. If your job requires a specific eye protection standard, confirm it is printed on the glasses before you use them.

name: Kask Replacement Hardware for Super Plasma Visors
title: Kask Super Plasma Visor Replacement Hardware
h1: Kask Replacement Hardware for Super Plasma Visors
meta: Replacement hardware for Kask Super Plasma visors: the small parts that hold a visor to the helmet. When to replace them and how to check your visor setup.
tagline: Spare mounting parts to keep a Kask Super Plasma visor tight and working.
summary: This Kask Super Plasma visor hardware kit replaces the small parts that attach a visor to the helmet. When a pivot works loose or a part goes missing in the brush, a hardware kit is cheaper than a new visor and gets the helmet back in service.
highlights: Replaces worn or lost visor mounting parts
For Kask Super Plasma visor setups
Cheaper than replacing the whole visor
Keeps the visor from flopping down mid-cut
Worth keeping a spare set in the gear bag

p: A visor gets flipped up and down dozens of times a day, knocked by limbs, and tossed in the truck with the rest of the gear. Over time the parts that hold it to the helmet loosen, crack or simply fall off. A visor that will not stay up, or drops into your face when you look down to make a cut, is more than an annoyance.
This kit gives you the replacement parts to rebuild the mount instead of buying a new visor. Check the listing against your helmet and visor model before ordering so you get the right pieces.

It is worth ordering a spare set before you need it. Small parts tend to go missing on the job, often when you are a long drive from the shop, and a visor that will not stay put usually ends up left in the truck. Swapping hardware takes a few minutes in the yard with the helmet on the tailgate.

Follow Kask's instructions when you swap parts, and do not modify or drill the helmet shell to make anything fit. Once installed, the visor should hold its position when raised and sit evenly when lowered.

Inspect the rest of the helmet while you are at it: the shell, the suspension and the chin strap. Replace a helmet after a significant impact or as the manufacturer directs. More visors and mounts are in our eye protection section.

faq.q: Will this hardware fit my Zenith?
faq.a: The kit is listed for Super Plasma visors. Check the parts against your helmet and visor model before ordering, as Kask's visor systems differ between models.

faq.q: When should I replace the visor itself?
faq.a: Replace the visor when the mesh is torn, bent, or clogged with damage, or a clear lens is scratched or cracked in your line of sight.

name: Kask Super Plasma Mesh Visor Carrier Adapter
title: Kask Super Plasma Mesh Visor Carrier Adapter
h1: Kask Super Plasma Mesh Visor Carrier Adapter
meta: The Kask Super Plasma visor adapter mounts a mesh visor carrier to your helmet so you can add face protection for saw work. Fit notes and setup tips.
tagline: Adapter that lets you mount a mesh visor carrier on a Kask Super Plasma helmet.
summary: The Kask Super Plasma visor adapter is the bracket that connects a mesh visor carrier to the helmet. If you climb or run a saw in a Super Plasma and want a full face screen, this is one of the parts that makes the setup work.
highlights: Mounts a mesh visor carrier to the Super Plasma
Turns a climbing helmet into a saw-ready setup
Visor flips up when you do not need it
Works alongside helmet-mounted ear defenders
Kask part made for Kask helmets

p: The Super Plasma is a popular climbing helmet, but out of the box it has no face screen. Adding a mesh visor makes it suitable for running a top-handle saw in the tree or a rear-handle saw on the ground, where chips and small branches come straight at your face.

This adapter is the link between the helmet and the visor carrier. Pair it with a mesh visor and, if you need them, Kask ear defenders that clip to the same helmet. Many users also wear safety glasses under the mesh to catch fine dust. See our eye protection range for visors and glasses.

A visor adds a little weight to the front of the helmet, so adjust the suspension and chin strap after you fit it. The helmet should stay level when you look down to make a cut and should not tip forward when the visor is lowered.
Check that your helmet model and visor carrier match this adapter before ordering, and install it following Kask's instructions without modifying the shell.
Before each day, make sure the visor raises and lowers cleanly and stays where you put it. A loose adapter is easy to tighten in the yard and a pain to deal with in the canopy.
If you share helmets across a crew, label the parts. Adapters and visors look similar between models, and mixing them up is a common reason a visor will not lock.

faq.q: Does this include a visor?
faq.a: Treat it as the adapter only unless the listing says otherwise. You will need a compatible mesh visor carrier and screen.

faq.q: Can I still use ear defenders?
faq.a: Yes, Kask's ear defenders are designed to mount to the Super Plasma alongside a visor setup. Check that the parts you choose are listed as compatible.

name: Kask Zenith Zen Visor Carrier
title: Kask Zenith Zen Visor Carrier for Saw Work
meta: The Kask Zenith visor carrier lets you fit a face screen to a Zenith helmet for saw and chipper work. What it does, what it fits and how to keep it working.
tagline: Visor carrier for mounting a face screen on the Kask Zenith helmet.
summary: The Kask Zenith visor carrier is the frame that holds a mesh or clear screen on a Zenith helmet. It lets a ground worker or climber add face protection for saw work and swing it up out of the way between cuts.
highlights: Mounts a face screen to the Kask Zenith
Flips up between cuts
Accepts compatible Kask mesh or clear screens
Works with Kask helmet-mounted ear defenders
Replaces a cracked or worn carrier

p: The carrier is the frame that holds the screen and pivots on the helmet. On the Zenith it lets you add a mesh screen for chainsaw and chipper work, or a clear one when you want to keep fine debris and spray off your face.

If your current carrier is cracked or will not hold its position, replacing it is a simple way to get the helmet back to full use. It also lets you convert a bare Zenith into a saw helmet. Look through our eye protection section for screens and glasses to go with it.

Ground crews on the Zenith often run a mesh screen most of the day and swap to clear for stump grinding, where fine debris is constant. Having a spare carrier set up with the second screen makes that swap quick, rather than fiddling with screens in the field.
Confirm the carrier and screen are listed for your Zenith version before you buy, and install them following Kask's instructions. Do not drill or modify the shell.
Clean the screen and carrier after sappy or dusty days and check the pivots for play. A mesh screen does not stop all fine dust, so pair it with safety glasses when cutting dry wood.
Store the helmet with the visor raised so the screen does not get pressed against other gear in the truck.

faq.q: Does the carrier come with a screen?
faq.a: Check the listing. Carriers are often sold separately from screens so you can choose mesh or clear.

faq.q: Will this fit a Super Plasma?
faq.a: It is listed for the Zenith. Super Plasma helmets use their own visor adapter, so match parts to your helmet model.

name: Pfanner Protos Helmet Clear Plastic Integrated Visor
title: Pfanner Protos Clear Integrated Visor
h1: Pfanner Protos Helmet Clear Plastic Integrated Visor
meta: A Pfanner Protos clear visor for the integrated helmet: replace a scratched lens or add a clear option for chipping and grinding. Fit and care notes inside.
tagline: Clear replacement visor for the Pfanner Protos integrated helmet.
summary: This Pfanner Protos clear visor is a clear plastic screen for the Protos integrated helmet. Swap it in when your current lens is scratched, or keep it as the clear option for chipping, stump grinding and other jobs where mesh lets too much fine debris through.
highlights: Clear plastic screen for the Protos integrated helmet
Keeps fine chips and dust off your face
Good choice for chipping and stump grinding
Replaces a scratched or cracked lens
Pfanner part for Pfanner helmets

body.h: When a clear visor beats mesh
p: Mesh visors are the standard for saw work because they do not fog and you can see through them in any light. But mesh lets fine dust through, and on a stump grinder or chipper that dust is constant. A clear visor stops it, which is why many Protos owners keep both and swap as the job changes.

Clear visors also make sense for spraying and for anyone tired of fine sawdust in their eyes. Pair it with safety glasses if your job calls for them. Browse more eye protection for mesh screens and glasses.
A clear visor is also handy when cutting with the sun low, since mesh can create glare and shadows that make it harder to read the kerf.
Install the visor following Pfanner's instructions for your version of the Protos and check that it locks in the up and down positions.
Wash it with water and a soft cloth; wiping off dry sawdust scratches clear plastic quickly. Replace it when scratches or cracks are in your line of sight.

Keep the clear visor in a soft bag when it is not on the helmet. Loose in a gear bin, it picks up scratches fast, and a scratched clear lens is harder to see through than a worn mesh one. Some users mark the date on a strip of tape when they fit a new visor so they know how long it has been in service.

faq.q: Does a clear visor fog up?
faq.a: It can in cold or humid weather, especially when you are working hard. Many users keep a mesh visor for saw work and swap to clear for chipping and grinding.

faq.q: Will this fit an older Protos?
faq.a: Pfanner has updated the Protos over the years. Check your helmet version against the listing before ordering.

name: Pfanner Protos Integrated Visor Mesh Screen (G16)
title: Pfanner Protos G16 Mesh Visor Screen
h1: Pfanner Protos Integrated Visor Mesh Screen (G16)
meta: The Pfanner Protos G16 mesh visor is a replacement screen for the integrated helmet, built for chainsaw work. Fit, care and when to replace a worn mesh visor.
tagline: Replacement mesh screen for the Pfanner Protos integrated helmet.
summary: The Pfanner Protos G16 mesh visor is the replacement mesh screen for the Protos integrated helmet. It is the screen most climbers and saw hands run day to day, and it is worth replacing once the mesh gets bent, torn or caked with pitch.
highlights: Mesh screen for the Protos integrated helmet
G16 mesh version
Does not fog like a clear lens
Stops chips and small branches
Swap in when the old mesh is damaged

p: A mesh visor is the standard face screen for chainsaw work. It does not fog, you can see through it in shade and sun, and it stops the chips and twigs that come off the bar. On the Protos it rides in the integrated mount and tucks up into the helmet when you do not need it.
Mesh does let fine dust through, so many users wear safety glasses underneath when cutting dry wood. Our eye protection section has glasses and clear screens if you want a backup.

Mesh visors also handle rain better than clear lenses, since water runs through rather than beading across your view. That makes mesh the default for most climbers in mixed weather, with a clear screen saved for chipping and grinding.
Replace the screen when the mesh is torn, dented into your field of view, or clogged with pitch you cannot clean out. A damaged mesh can also rub or catch when you raise it.
Check your Protos version against the listing before ordering, and follow Pfanner's instructions for removal and fitting.

Some climbers keep a spare mesh screen in their gear bag. If a branch bends the mesh mid-job, a fresh screen gets you back to work in a few minutes rather than finishing the day without face protection. Clean pitch off the old screen promptly, because it hardens and becomes much harder to remove once it sets.

faq.q: What does G16 mean?
faq.a: It identifies this mesh visor version in Pfanner's range. Match it to your helmet using the listing or Pfanner's fit guide.

faq.q: How do I clean pitch off the mesh?
faq.a: A little citrus or resin cleaner and a soft brush usually works. Avoid harsh solvents that could damage the frame, and rinse with water afterward.

name: 6 ft Reinforced Cross Arm Strap
title: 6 ft Reinforced Cross Arm Strap Anchor
meta: A 6 ft reinforced cross arm strap wraps a beam, pole or limb to make a quick anchor point. How cross arm straps are used, inspected and matched to your system.
tagline: A 6 ft wrap-around anchor strap for beams, poles and solid limbs.
summary: A cross arm strap is a reinforced webbing strap with a D-ring or loop at each end that wraps around a beam, pole or limb to create an anchor point. This 6 ft version gives enough wrap for most structural members and many tree stems.
highlights: 6 ft length for wrapping beams, poles and stems
Reinforced webbing with wear protection
Quick anchor without tying knots
Packs small in a gear bag
Useful for aerial lift and structure work

body.h: How a cross arm strap works
p: You wrap the strap around the anchor, pass one end through the other, and clip into the end ring. It cinches down on the member and gives you a clean connection point with no knots to tie. Utility crews use them on cross arms and poles; tree crews use them as quick anchors on structures and as a wrap on a stem when a rope sling is not handy.

The reinforced section protects the webbing where it bears on edges and bark. Even so, keep it off sharp corners and keep it away from the saw. See our fall protection range for lanyards and other anchors.

A 6 ft strap gives enough wrap for most beams and poles, plus many stems. If the anchor is too small for the strap to cinch properly, choke it with more wraps only if the manufacturer allows, or choose a shorter strap.
Check the webbing for cuts, burns, abrasion and chemical damage, and the hardware for cracks or distortion, before each use. Retire it after a fall or if you find damage.

Use it only as the manufacturer's instructions allow and within its rated strength. Life-support and fall-arrest gear must meet the applicable standard, including ANSI Z133 for tree work, and should be used only by trained workers.

faq.q: Can I use this as a tree climbing anchor?
faq.a: Only if the manufacturer's instructions allow it for that use and the anchor itself is sound. Many climbers prefer a purpose-built friction saver or anchor sling for the tree.

faq.q: Why reinforced?
faq.a: The reinforcement protects the webbing where it bears against the anchor, which is where straps usually wear first.

name: Fred the Rescue Dummy Rubber Filler
title: Fred the Rescue Dummy Rubber Filler
h1: Fred the Rescue Dummy Rubber Filler
meta: Rubber filler for Fred the rescue dummy adds weight back to a training manikin for aerial rescue practice. How crews use rescue dummies and keep them realistic.
tagline: Rubber filler to bring a Fred rescue training dummy back up to weight.
summary: This rescue dummy filler is the rubber fill used to give Fred the rescue dummy its weight. Aerial rescue drills only teach the right lessons when the dummy is heavy enough to feel like a real person, and the filler is how you keep it that way.
highlights: Rubber fill for the Fred rescue dummy
Restores realistic weight for drills
Lets you adjust weight for different scenarios
Keeps a training manikin in service
Supports regular aerial rescue practice
specs: Rubber filler for rescue training dummy

p: Aerial rescue drills are about moving a limp, heavy person out of a tree or bucket. If the dummy is light, the lowering setup, the friction and the effort all feel easier than they will on a real day. Rubber filler brings the dummy up to a weight that makes practice honest.

Crews often add or remove fill to simulate different climbers, which is a good way to test a rescue system with more than one load. Check our fall protection section for the rescue and fall-arrest gear you train with.

Store the dummy dry between sessions. Moisture adds weight unevenly and can break down the fill and the dummy's covering over time. Check seams and closures before each drill so filler does not leak out mid-rescue, which is a mess to clean up and changes the weight halfway through the exercise.

Drill aerial rescue on a regular schedule and with the gear you actually carry. Rig for the dummy as if it were a person, inspect all life-support equipment before use, and have a trained, qualified person run the session.
Follow ANSI Z133 and your employer's rescue plan. Confirm the filler amount and fit with the dummy's maker before filling.

faq.q: How much filler do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the dummy and the target weight. Check with the dummy's manufacturer for its fill capacity and intended weight.

faq.q: Why not just use sandbags?
faq.a: Rubber fill spreads through the dummy and moves more like a body, while sandbags shift and concentrate weight in odd places.

name: Petzl ASAP Lock Fall Arrester
title: Petzl ASAP Lock Fall Arrester: Specs and Uses
meta: The Petzl ASAP Lock is a mobile fall arrester for a backup rope that can be locked in place. How it works, rope fit, and where it fits in an arborist kit.
tagline: Mobile rope fall arrester with a locking function for backup on a second line.
summary: The Petzl ASAP Lock is a mobile fall arrester that rides a separate backup rope and locks if you fall. Its locking function lets you fix it in place on the rope, which is useful when you are working near the edge or want to limit how far it can travel.
highlights: Follows you up and down the backup rope
Locking function fixes it at a point on the rope
Opens to install anywhere on the rope
Used with a Petzl energy absorber in fall arrest
Compact and quick to clip in

p: The ASAP Lock runs on a separate backup line and slides freely as you move. If you fall or lose control, it grabs the rope and stops you. The lock function lets you hold it at a fixed point on the rope so it will not slide down past you, which is handy when you are setting up near an edge or working from a structure.

In fall-arrest use it is paired with a Petzl energy absorber, such as the ASAP'SORBER, between the device and your harness. Read the instructions for the exact connector and absorber combinations it is approved with. More options are in our fall protection section.

In tree work the ASAP Lock tends to show up in situations that borrow from rope access, such as working from structures, towers or cranes, or where a site rule calls for a separate backup line. For ordinary canopy climbing, most arborists rely on their primary climbing system and training rather than a mobile fall arrester.
Use it only on the rope types and diameters Petzl lists for it, and check the device locks correctly on your rope before every use. Inspect the cam, body and connector for wear, cracks and debris.

This is life-support equipment. It must be used per the manufacturer's instructions and the applicable standard, including ANSI Z133 for tree work, and only by people trained in rope access and rescue.

faq.q: Can I use the ASAP Lock as my climbing device?
faq.a: No. It is a backup fall arrester on a separate line, not a primary ascent or descent device.

faq.q: What rope does it work on?
faq.a: Petzl lists semi-static rope in the 10 to 13 mm range. Check the current instructions for the exact compatible ropes.

name: Buckingham Blood Stopper Kit (Green)
title: Buckingham Blood Stopper Kit for Tree Crews
meta: The Buckingham Blood Stopper Kit puts bleeding control supplies in a pouch you carry on a saddle or belt. What it is for and how crews should carry and train.
tagline: Wearable bleeding control kit for chainsaw and climbing crews.
summary: The Buckingham Blood Stopper Kit is a compact bleeding control pouch built to ride on a saddle or belt where you can reach it fast. Chainsaw cuts bleed hard and quickly, and having the supplies on your body instead of in the truck can save critical minutes.
highlights: Bleeding control supplies in one pouch
Green pouch that is easy to spot
Mounts on a saddle or belt
Keeps first aid within reach aloft
Made by Buckingham for tree crews

body.h: Why carry it on your body
p: A chainsaw cut to the leg or arm can bleed fast. If the only kit is in the truck cab, a climber in the tree or a groundie at the back of a lot loses minutes getting to it. A blood stopper kit on the saddle or belt keeps the supplies where they are needed.

Check the listing for the exact contents of the kit you buy and add items your crew trains with, such as a tourniquet, if they are not included. Browse our first aid section for refills and larger kits.

The green color makes it easy to tell apart from other saddle pouches, which matters when someone else has to grab it from you in a hurry. Talk through where everyone on the crew keeps their kit so nobody has to search.
Supplies only help if people know how to use them. Get the crew trained in first aid and bleeding control, and practice getting the kit open with gloves on.
Check the pouch regularly, replace anything used or expired, and keep it dry. Follow your employer's emergency plan and call emergency services for any serious injury.
Keep a matching kit in the truck and chipper so the ground crew has one close by too.

faq.q: What is inside the kit?
faq.a: Contents can change, so check the listing. It is built around bleeding control supplies in a pouch you can wear.

faq.q: Where should I mount it?
faq.a: Somewhere both you and a coworker can reach quickly, such as the side of your saddle or belt, and not under other gear.

name: Weaver Orange First Aid Pouch
title: Weaver Orange First Aid Pouch for Saddles
meta: The Weaver first aid pouch is a bright orange belt or saddle pouch for carrying basic first aid supplies on the job. Sizing, mounting and what to keep inside.
tagline: Bright orange pouch for keeping first aid supplies on your saddle or belt.
summary: The Weaver first aid pouch is a bright orange pouch made to carry first aid supplies on a saddle or work belt. The color makes it easy to find in the gear pile and easy for a coworker to spot on you in an emergency.
highlights: High-visibility orange
Mounts on a saddle or belt
Keeps first aid on the climber, not in the truck
Durable Weaver construction
Easy for coworkers to find

p: When someone gets hurt aloft, the climber is often the first responder. A pouch on the saddle means bandages and bleeding control are already up there. The orange color matters too: a coworker should be able to see where the kit is without digging through gear.
Check the listing to see whether the pouch ships with supplies or empty, then stock it with what your crew is trained to use. Our first aid section has kits and refills.

Weaver is known for saddles and climbing accessories that hold up to daily abuse, and the pouch is made to the same standard. Mount it on the side of your saddle or belt where it will not interfere with your lanyard, saw or hip-mounted gear, and where a coworker can reach it if you cannot.
Go through the pouch on a schedule. Replace anything used, wet or out of date, and make sure the closure still holds.
Get trained in first aid and bleeding control, and follow your employer's emergency plan. Call emergency services for any serious injury.

A useful starting point for contents is bleeding control supplies, gauze, adhesive bandages, gloves and tape. Add anything your crew's training or local regulations call for, and keep a list of contents inside the flap so restocking is quick and nothing gets forgotten.

faq.q: Does it come stocked?
faq.a: Check the listing for the version you are buying. Some pouches are sold empty so you can fill them with your own supplies.

faq.q: Why orange?
faq.a: High-visibility color makes the kit easy to find in a gear bag and easy for a coworker to spot on your saddle.

name: 3M Peltor X3P3E Helmet-Mounted Hearing Protectors
title: 3M Peltor X3P3E Helmet-Mounted Earmuffs
meta: The 3M Peltor X3P3E clips to a slotted helmet to give you earmuffs for saw and chipper work. How the cap mount works, fit tips and when to replace pads.
tagline: Peltor X-series earmuffs that clip into slotted helmets for saw and chipper work.
summary: The 3M Peltor X3P3E is a helmet-mounted version of the Peltor X3 earmuff that clips into the side slots of many hard hats and climbing helmets. It gives saw operators and chipper crews solid hearing protection that swings away when they need to talk.
highlights: Peltor X3 muff on a helmet attachment
Clips into standard helmet slots
Swings out to a rest position when not needed
Replaceable cushions and foam liners
Good mid-level choice for saw and chipper noise

p: The X-series is 3M's line of passive earmuffs, and the X3 sits in the middle-to-upper part of the range. The P3E attachment lets it clip into the slots on many hard hats and some climbing helmets, so you get muffs that stay with the helmet and flip up when you need to hear the ground crew.
It is a practical pick for running a saw, feeding a chipper or working near a stump grinder. Check the noise reduction rating printed on the product against the noise levels your crew works in.
Helmet mounts have one big advantage over headband muffs: they cannot be left in the truck. When the muffs live on the helmet, putting them on is a flip of the cup rather than a decision.

Make sure the muffs seal fully around your ears. Glasses arms, hats and hair under the cushion all reduce protection, so keep the seal clean. Wipe the cushions after sweaty days and replace them and the foam inserts when they harden, crack or flatten.

Check that the P3E attachment is listed as compatible with your helmet before ordering. Noise exposure from saws, chippers and grinders adds up quickly, so wear hearing protection whenever the equipment is running. More options are in our hearing protection section.

faq.q: Will it fit my climbing helmet?
faq.a: It fits helmets with standard accessory slots. Many climbing helmets use their own mounts, so check compatibility before you buy.

faq.q: Can I replace the cushions?
faq.a: Yes, 3M sells hygiene kits with replacement cushions and foam inserts for the X-series.

name: Kask SC1 Green Ear Defenders (Super Plasma and Zenith)
title: Kask SC1 Ear Defenders for Super Plasma and Zenith
meta: Kask SC1 ear defenders clip to the Super Plasma and Zenith helmets for saw, chipper and blower work. Fit notes, how they compare to the SC3, and care tips.
tagline: Green helmet-mounted ear defenders for Kask Super Plasma and Zenith helmets.
summary: The Kask SC1 ear defenders are green helmet-mounted earmuffs made for the Super Plasma and Zenith helmets. They give climbers and ground workers hearing protection that stays on the helmet and flips up when it is time to talk.
highlights: Mounts to Kask Super Plasma and Zenith helmets
Flips up to a rest position
Lighter, lower-profile option than the SC3
Replaceable cushions
Green color for easy ID

p: Kask offers its helmet ear defenders in more than one level. The SC1 is the lighter, lower-profile option, while the SC3 gives more attenuation for louder or longer exposure. A climber who runs a top-handle saw in short bursts may prefer the SC1 for comfort; someone feeding a chipper all day may want more.
Check the noise reduction rating on the product and compare it to the noise levels you work in. Kask's mount system lets you use them with a visor on the same helmet.
Because the defenders mount directly to the helmet, they do not press on the sides of your head like a headband muff, which helps when you wear them under a cold-weather liner.

Make sure the muffs seal fully around your ears. Glasses arms, hats and hair under the cushion all reduce protection, so keep the seal clean. Wipe the cushions after sweaty days and replace them and the foam inserts when they harden, crack or flatten.

Check that the SC1 is listed as compatible with your helmet before ordering. Noise exposure from saws, chippers and grinders adds up quickly, so wear hearing protection whenever the equipment is running. More options are in our hearing protection section.

faq.q: Do these fit other helmets?
faq.a: They are made for Kask's Super Plasma and Zenith. Other helmets use different mounts.

faq.q: Can I run a visor too?
faq.a: Yes, Kask designs its ear defenders to work alongside its visor setups on these helmets.

name: Kask SC3 Orange Ear Defenders (Super Plasma and Zenith)
title: Kask SC3 Ear Defenders for Super Plasma and Zenith
meta: Kask SC3 ear defenders are the higher-protection Kask helmet muffs for the Super Plasma and Zenith, made for saws and chippers. Fit, care and SC1 comparison.
tagline: Higher-attenuation helmet ear defenders for Kask Super Plasma and Zenith.
summary: The Kask SC3 ear defenders are orange helmet-mounted earmuffs for the Super Plasma and Zenith, and the higher-protection choice in Kask's range. They suit crews that spend long days around saws, chippers and stump grinders.
highlights: Mounts to Kask Super Plasma and Zenith helmets
More attenuation than the SC1
Flips up to a rest position
Replaceable cushions
Orange color for easy ID

body.h: When to step up to the SC3
p: Hearing damage builds from long exposure, not just loud moments. If you are feeding a chipper, running a saw on the ground all day or working next to a grinder, more attenuation makes sense, and that is where the SC3 fits.

The trade-off is a slightly bulkier muff than the SC1. Climbers who care most about weight sometimes pick the SC1; ground crews often go with the SC3. Check the rating printed on the product against your noise levels.

Orange also makes it easy to tell which helmets on a crew carry the higher-protection muffs. Because they mount to the helmet rather than a headband, they stay put when you bend to feed brush or look up to watch a climber, and they are always there when the machine starts.

Make sure the muffs seal fully around your ears. Glasses arms, hats and hair under the cushion all reduce protection, so keep the seal clean. Wipe the cushions after sweaty days and replace them and the foam inserts when they harden, crack or flatten.

Check that the SC3 is listed as compatible with your helmet before ordering. Noise exposure from saws, chippers and grinders adds up quickly, so wear hearing protection whenever the equipment is running. More options are in our hearing protection section.

faq.q: How is the SC3 different from the SC1?
faq.a: The SC3 offers more noise reduction, at the cost of a little more size and weight.

faq.q: Will they fit my Kask Plasma Work helmet?
faq.a: They are listed for the Super Plasma and Zenith. Check Kask's compatibility list for other models.

name: 3M Peltor Optime 105 Helmet-Mounted Earmuff
title: Peltor Optime 105 Helmet-Mounted Earmuff
meta: The Peltor Optime 105 helmet-mounted earmuff is the top passive muff in the Optime line, built for chippers, grinders and saws. Fit, care and how it compares.
tagline: The highest-protection Optime muff, made to clip onto slotted helmets.
summary: The Peltor Optime 105 helmet-mounted earmuff is the highest-attenuation model in 3M's Optime line, built on an attachment that clips into slotted helmets. It is a long-time favorite for chipper, grinder and saw crews who are around loud equipment all day.
highlights: Top of the Optime passive range
Helmet attachment for slotted hard hats
Double-shell design for low-frequency noise
Flips up when you need to talk
Replaceable cushions and liners

p: The Optime line comes in three levels, and the 105 is the one with the most protection. Its larger cups are designed to handle low-frequency engine noise, which makes it a good match for chippers, stump grinders and big saws.

The trade-off is size: these muffs are bulkier than the lighter Optime models. If you run equipment all day, the extra protection is usually worth it. Compare the noise reduction rating on the product to your actual exposure.
Helmet-mounted muffs stay with the hard hat, so they are always there when the chipper starts. Flip them out to the rest position to talk, then back down when the noise starts again.

Make sure the muffs seal fully around your ears. Glasses arms, hats and hair under the cushion all reduce protection, so keep the seal clean. Wipe the cushions after sweaty days and replace them and the foam inserts when they harden, crack or flatten.

Check that the helmet attachment is listed as compatible with your helmet before ordering. Noise exposure from saws, chippers and grinders adds up quickly, so wear hearing protection whenever the equipment is running. More options are in our hearing protection section.

faq.q: Which Optime is the strongest?
faq.a: The Optime 105 is the highest-protection model in the Optime line.

faq.q: Will it fit my climbing helmet?
faq.a: It fits helmets with standard accessory slots. Check your helmet before ordering, as some climbing helmets use their own mounts.

name: Pfanner Protos Ear Protection Pad Replacement
title: Pfanner Protos Ear Protection Replacement Pads
h1: Pfanner Protos Ear Protection Pad Replacement
meta: Replacement Pfanner Protos ear pads restore the seal on your Protos helmet muffs. Why worn pads cut protection, when to swap them and how to keep muffs clean.
tagline: Fresh cushions to restore the seal on Pfanner Protos helmet ear muffs.
summary: These Pfanner Protos ear pads replace the cushions on the Protos helmet's ear protection. Worn pads lose their seal and let noise in, so swapping them is one of the cheapest ways to keep your hearing protection doing its job.
highlights: Replacement cushions for Protos ear muffs
Restores the seal around your ears
Cleaner and more comfortable than worn pads
Simple swap without tools
Pfanner part for Pfanner helmets

p: An earmuff only protects as well as it seals. Sweat, sun and sawdust harden the cushions over a season, and once they crack or flatten, noise leaks in around the edge. You may not notice the drop, but your ears do.
Replacing the pads brings the muffs back to how they felt new. Many users swap them once or twice a year depending on use, and sooner if they are sweating heavily every day.

Fresh pads also make long days more comfortable. Cracked or hardened cushions press unevenly and rub, and people tend to lift muffs off when they are uncomfortable, which defeats the purpose. A new set costs less than most saw chains and makes a noticeable difference in both comfort and seal.
Check that the pads match your version of the Protos before ordering and follow Pfanner's instructions to swap them. Replace any foam inserts at the same time if they are worn.
Wipe the cushions after sweaty days and keep them out of direct sun when the helmet is stored. See more in our hearing protection section.
Keep a spare set in the truck if you sweat a lot or share helmets across a crew, so pads can be swapped on the spot rather than waiting for the next order.

faq.q: How often should I replace them?
faq.a: When they harden, crack, flatten or will not seal. For daily use that is often once or twice a year.

faq.q: Do these fit all Protos helmets?
faq.a: Pfanner has made more than one Protos version. Match the pads to your helmet using the listing.

name: 3M Peltor Optime Helmet-Mounted Muffs (Yellow)
title: Yellow Peltor Optime Helmet-Mounted Earmuffs
meta: The yellow Peltor Optime helmet-mounted earmuffs are the lightest Optime model, made for moderate noise and long wear. Where they fit and how to care for them.
tagline: Lightweight yellow Optime earmuffs that clip onto slotted helmets.
summary: These yellow Peltor Optime helmet-mounted earmuffs are the lightest model in 3M's Optime line. They suit moderate noise and long wear, like blower work, hand cleanup and light saw use, where a heavier muff would be overkill.
highlights: Lightest model in the Optime line
Helmet attachment for slotted hard hats
Comfortable for all-day wear
Flips up when not needed
Replaceable cushions and liners

body.h: Matching the muff to the noise
p: The Optime range comes in three levels. The yellow muffs are the lightest and have the lowest attenuation, which suits moderate noise. For a chipper or stump grinder you will usually want a higher model like the Optime 105.

That makes the yellow Optime a good choice for groundies doing cleanup, running a blower or working around but not right next to a saw. Check the noise reduction rating on the product against your exposure.

Lighter muffs also mean less weight on the helmet and less pressure on your head, which some people find makes it easier to keep them on all day. Protection you actually wear beats higher protection left in the truck.

Make sure the muffs seal fully around your ears. Glasses arms, hats and hair under the cushion all reduce protection, so keep the seal clean. Wipe the cushions after sweaty days and replace them and the foam inserts when they harden, crack or flatten.

Check that the helmet attachment is listed as compatible with your helmet before ordering. Noise exposure from saws, chippers and grinders adds up quickly, so wear hearing protection whenever the equipment is running. More options are in our hearing protection section.

faq.q: Are these enough for chipper work?
faq.a: Usually not for long exposure. Chippers and grinders call for higher protection, such as the Optime 105.

faq.q: Do they fit any hard hat?
faq.a: They fit helmets with standard accessory slots. Check your helmet before ordering.

name: 1/2 in Eye Bolt for Tree Cabling
title: 1/2 in Eye Bolt for Tree Cabling and Bracing
h1: 1/2 in Eye Bolt for Tree Cabling
meta: A 1/2 in eye bolt is the through-bolt anchor for many tree cabling systems. How eye bolts are used in cabling, sizing to the tree, and installation basics.
tagline: A 1/2 in through-bolt anchor for tree cabling and support systems.
summary: A 1/2 in eye bolt for tree cabling is a through-bolt anchor that passes through the limb and gives the cable a strong attachment point. It is one of the standard anchors for steel cable systems on medium-sized leaders.
highlights: 1/2 in diameter through-bolt
Forged eye for cable attachment
Used with a nut and washer on the far side
Standard anchor for steel cable systems
Pair with matching thimbles and cable

body.h: Where an eye bolt fits in a cabling system
p: In a steel cable system, each end of the cable needs a solid anchor in the tree. A through-bolted eye bolt is one of the most common: you drill straight through the limb, run the bolt through, and secure it with a washer and nut on the far side. The cable then attaches to the eye, usually with a thimble and a preformed dead-end grip or wire rope clips.
The 1/2 in size suits a range of medium leaders. Larger stems and heavier loads call for bigger hardware. Find matching cable and fittings in our cabling hardware section.
Eye bolts are typically galvanized or otherwise corrosion-resistant so they hold up in the tree for years. Check the listing for the bolt length and whether a nut and washer are included.
Choose the bolt length to pass fully through the limb with enough thread for the washer and nut. Drill a hole matched to the bolt, set the eye in line with the cable, and avoid drilling into decay.
Cabling should be designed and installed by a qualified arborist following ANSI A300 and ANSI Z133. Inspect systems regularly and keep records.
Plan the cable height and anchor spacing before drilling; once a hole is in the tree it cannot be undone.

faq.q: What length do I need?
faq.a: Long enough to pass through the limb at the install point with room for the washer and nut. Measure the stem diameter where you will drill.

faq.q: Can I use it with synthetic cable?
faq.a: Some synthetic systems use their own anchors. Follow the cable maker's instructions for compatible hardware.

name: 1.8 mm Throw Line
title: 1.8mm Throw Line for Setting Climbing Lines
meta: A 1.8mm throw line is the thin, slick cord arborists use with a throw weight to set climbing and rigging lines. Thin vs thick line, storage, and care tips.
tagline: Thin, slick throw line for setting climbing and rigging lines high in the canopy.
summary: A 1.8mm throw line is the thin, low-friction cord you tie to a throw weight to set a climbing or rigging line in the canopy. At 1.8 mm it is on the thin side for throw line, which helps it fly farther and slip over unions easily.
highlights: 1.8 mm diameter for long, clean throws
Slick surface slides over bark and unions
Ties to a standard throw weight
Works with a throw cube or bag
For pulling up climbing and rigging lines

p: Throw line comes in a few diameters, and thinner line weighs less and drags less through the air, so the weight carries farther. It also slides over branch unions with less friction, which makes isolating a tie-in point easier. The trade-off is that very thin line tangles more and is harder to handle with gloves on.
At 1.8 mm, this line is on the thinner side. Use a cube or bag to keep it organized, and pair it with a throw weight sized to your canopy. See more in our throw line section.

Thin line is also less likely to damage bark or pull small branches down as it runs, and it takes up less space in a throw cube. Practice a clean throw-and-retrieve routine on the ground first so that the line does not snarl the first time you need to set a high tie-in.

Throw line is for setting lines, not for life support or lifting loads. Once the throw line is set, use it to pull up your climbing line, then inspect the tie-in point from the ground before you commit to it.
Keep the line clean and dry, check for nicks and glazed spots, and cut out damaged sections. Store it in a cube so it pays out cleanly on the next throw.

faq.q: Is 1.8 mm too thin?
faq.a: It is thinner than many throw lines and some climbers love it for distance. If you struggle with tangles or gloves, a slightly thicker line is easier to handle.

faq.q: How long should my throw line be?
faq.a: Long enough to go up and over your highest tie-in and back to the ground. Many arborists carry around 180 ft or more.

name: 10.5 mm Replacement Rope Bridge
title: 10.5mm Replacement Rope Bridge for Saddles
meta: A 10.5mm replacement rope bridge restores the main attachment point on a climbing saddle. When to replace a bridge, how to check fit, and inspection basics.
tagline: Replacement 10.5 mm rope bridge for arborist climbing saddles.
summary: A replacement rope bridge restores the main attachment point on a climbing saddle that uses a rope bridge. This one is 10.5 mm cord, and it is a wear item that should be swapped well before it looks worn out.
highlights: 10.5 mm rope bridge
Replaces a worn saddle bridge
Restores the saddle's main connection point
Keeps your saddle in service
Check fit to your saddle model

p: The bridge is the part of the saddle your climbing system connects to, and on many modern saddles it is a length of rope. Every movement slides your carabiner or ring along it, so it wears faster than the rest of the saddle. Fuzzing, glazing, flat spots or a stiff section are all reasons to replace it.
Check that the length, diameter and end terminations match your saddle before ordering. Bridges are often model-specific. Our saddle parts section has more options.

Replacing the bridge on schedule is one of the cheapest ways to keep a saddle safe. Many climbers keep a spare in the gear bag so a worn bridge never becomes a reason to climb on it one more day. Mark the date you installed it on a tag or in your gear log.
Install the new bridge exactly as the saddle maker's instructions describe, including any stopper knots or terminations, and check it before every climb.
The bridge is life-support equipment. Use only parts approved for your saddle, follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and retire the bridge at the first sign of damage.
When you fit the new bridge, check the attachment points on the saddle for wear too. A fresh bridge will not help if the loops or rings it passes through are worn.

faq.q: How often should I replace my bridge?
faq.a: It depends on how much you climb. Inspect it before every climb and replace it when you see wear, glazing or damage, or as the saddle maker directs.

faq.q: Will a 10.5 mm bridge fit my saddle?
faq.a: Only if your saddle is designed for that diameter and length. Check the saddle maker's spec before ordering.

name: 10 mm Prusik Grab Lanyard Add-On Kit
title: 10mm Prusik Grab Lanyard Add-On Kit
h1: 10 mm Prusik Grab Lanyard Add-On Kit
meta: A 10mm prusik grab lanyard add-on kit adds a friction hitch adjuster to a rope lanyard so you can fine-tune your position. What is in it and how it is used.
tagline: Add a prusik adjuster to a rope lanyard for quick positioning changes.
summary: This prusik lanyard adjuster kit uses 10 mm hitch cord to turn a plain rope lanyard into an adjustable one. It is a simple, low-cost way to get fine control over your work positioning without buying a mechanical adjuster.
highlights: 10 mm hitch cord for the friction hitch
Turns a rope lanyard into an adjustable lanyard
Low-cost alternative to mechanical adjusters
Easy to inspect and replace
Works with a matching connector

body.h: How a prusik lanyard adjuster works
p: A friction hitch tied with hitch cord grips the lanyard rope when loaded and slides when you tend it. Clip it to your saddle and you can shorten or lengthen your lanyard with one hand while you work. Many climbers still prefer a hitch over a mechanical adjuster because it is light, cheap and easy to inspect.
The 10 mm cord suits common lanyard rope sizes. Check that it is compatible with your lanyard's diameter and cover before you set it up. See more in our lanyard kits section.

An adjustable lanyard is what lets you lean back into a cut at the right distance, then shorten up to move around a limb. Without an adjuster you end up re-tying or wrapping the lanyard, which is slower and easier to get wrong.
Tie and dress the hitch as you have been trained, and load test it close to the ground before relying on it. Watch for glazing, heat damage and wear on the cord.
This is life-support equipment. Use components that meet the applicable standard, follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and only climb with gear you have been trained to use.
Keep a spare length of hitch cord in your kit. Cords wear faster than lanyard rope, especially with heavy use, and swapping one out is quick.

faq.q: Which hitch should I tie?
faq.a: Use a hitch you have been trained on and that grips well on your lanyard rope. Test it low before climbing.

faq.q: Will it work on any lanyard?
faq.a: It depends on your lanyard rope diameter and construction. Check compatibility before setting it up.

name: 12 oz Throw Weight and Line Kit
title: 12 oz Throw Weight and Line Kit
h1: 12 oz Throw Weight and Line Kit
meta: A 12 oz throw weight kit pairs a weight with throw line to set climbing and rigging lines. Who the 12 oz size suits and how to keep the line tangle-free.
tagline: A 12 oz throw weight with line, ready to set climbing and rigging lines.
summary: This 12 oz throw weight kit puts a throw weight and throw line together so you can start setting lines right away. The 12 oz size is a common all-round choice that throws high without much effort and still drops through moderate foliage.
highlights: 12 oz throw weight
Throw line included
Ready to set climbing and rigging lines
Bright colors to find the weight in brush
Pairs with a throw cube or bag for storage

p: Throw weights range roughly from 8 oz to 16 oz. Lighter weights fly higher with less effort and pull thin line easily, but they can hang up and refuse to come down through dense foliage. Heavier weights punch through leaves and drop back to the ground better, but take more effort to throw high and can be harder on the tree and anyone nearby.

The 12 oz size is a common all-round choice that throws high without much effort and still drops through moderate foliage. Check the listing for the exact line length and diameter in the kit, and browse our throw line kits to compare sizes.

body.h: Throwing safely and keeping line tidy
p: Clear the drop zone before every throw and call it out. Never stand under the weight's path, and keep traffic and bystanders well back. Throw line and weights are for setting lines only, not for life support or lifting.

Flake the line into a cube or bag so it feeds without knots. Check the line for nicks and the weight for a worn ring or torn cover, and replace either if damaged. Inspect your tie-in point from the ground before climbing.
If you set lines often, a second weight and a throw cube let you keep one line ready while the other is in the tree.

faq.q: Is 12 oz right for me?
faq.a: The 12 oz size is a common all-round choice that throws high without much effort and still drops through moderate foliage.

faq.q: Does the kit include a storage cube?
faq.a: Check the listing for the exact contents. A cube or bag is worth having to keep the line from tangling.

name: 5/16 in Winch Line
title: 5/16 Winch Line: Synthetic Rope for Pulling
meta: A 5/16 winch line is a light synthetic pulling rope for portable winches and tree work. Why crews choose synthetic line, sizing, and inspection basics inside.
tagline: Light 5/16 in synthetic line for winching, pulling and tree work.
summary: A 5/16 winch line is a lightweight pulling rope sized for portable and vehicle winches used in tree work. Synthetic winch line is lighter and easier to handle than steel cable, and it does not leave broken wire strands to snag your gloves.
highlights: 5/16 in diameter
Lighter than steel cable
Easy to handle and splice
For winching, pulling and directional felling setups
Floats and stores compactly

p: Synthetic winch line is a fraction of the weight of steel cable of similar strength, so it is easier to drag to the anchor and safer when something lets go, because it stores less energy than wire. It is also kinder to hands, with no broken wire ends.

At 5/16 in, it suits smaller winches and pulling jobs such as dragging logs to the landing or adding a pull line on a lean. Check the listing for length, construction and rated strength, and compare with other lines in our rigging rope section.

Synthetic line does need more care than steel. It is weakened by heat, sharp edges, UV and chemicals, so keep it off hot exhausts and out of the sun when stored, and use chafe protection where it runs over an edge. A bag keeps it clean and ready.
Stay within the working load limit of the line and every piece of hardware in the system, and keep people out of the bight and line of pull. Protect the line from sharp edges, heat and abrasion.

Inspect it before every job for cut strands, glazing, fused spots and stiffness, and retire it when damaged. Train the crew in winching and rigging under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Can I put this on my truck winch?
faq.a: Only if the winch maker approves synthetic line and the drum, fairlead and ratings match. Check both the winch and line specs.

faq.q: What length does it come in?
faq.a: Check the listing for the lengths available.

name: 7/8 in Dead Eye Rigging Sling
title: 7/8 in Dead Eye Rigging Sling for Heavy Rigging
meta: A 7/8 in dead eye rigging sling is a heavy rope sling with a spliced eye for choking big wood and setting blocks. How it is used, sized and inspected on a job.
tagline: Heavy 7/8 in rope sling with a spliced eye for big-wood rigging.
summary: A dead eye rigging sling is a rope sling with a spliced eye at one end and a tail at the other, used to choke a stem or hang a block. This 7/8 in version is built for heavy rigging, where small slings would be undersized for the loads.
highlights: 7/8 in rope for heavy rigging
Spliced eye at one end
Chokes around a stem to make a rigging point
Used to hang blocks or choke pieces
Easy to inspect rope construction

body.h: How a dead eye sling is used
p: Wrap the sling around the spar, pass the tail through the eye, and pull it snug to make a choker that holds its place on a vertical stem. The tail then connects to a block or the lowering line. Dead eye slings are also used to choke the piece being cut so the rigging line attaches cleanly.
The 7/8 in size is for heavy work: big wood, big blocks and high dynamic loads. Check the listing for length and rated strength, and see our heavy-duty slings for other sizes.

Use a sling long enough to choke the stem with some tail left over to make the connection. Too short and you will not get a proper choke; too long and the block hangs low and the tail gets in the way. Many crews carry a few lengths so they can match the sling to the wood.
Match the sling to the rest of the system, including the block, rope and anchor, and stay within the working load limit of every component. Account for dynamic loads when dropping pieces.

Inspect the rope and splice before every job for cut strands, glazing, stiffness and core damage, and retire it when in doubt. Rig only with trained crews under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Dead eye or ring sling?
faq.a: A dead eye sling chokes using its own eye and connects through the tail. A ring sling uses a ring to choke. Both work; many crews carry both.

faq.q: Is 7/8 in overkill?
faq.a: For small pruning wood, yes. It is for heavy removals and large blocks where loads are high.

name: 8 mm Sirius Thimble Prusik
title: 8mm Sirius Thimble Prusik
meta: The 8mm Sirius thimble prusik is hitch cord with thimble-protected eyes for friction hitches on climbing or rigging lines. How it is used, fit and inspection.
tagline: 8 mm hitch cord with thimble eyes for friction hitches on climbing or rigging lines.
summary: The Sirius thimble prusik is a length of 8 mm cord with an eye at each end protected by a thimble. Thimble eyes hold their shape and resist wear at the connector, which makes this style popular for friction hitches on climbing systems and for rigging tie-offs.
highlights: 8 mm cord
Thimble-protected eyes at both ends
Eyes hold their shape at the connector
For friction hitches on compatible rope
Easy to inspect and replace
specs: Eye with thimble at each end

p: A plain sewn or spliced eye squeezes down on a carabiner and wears where it bears. A thimble keeps the eye open and spreads the load over the connector, so the eye lasts longer and the hitch sits consistently. That is why thimble prusiks are common for rope grabs on rigging lines and for climbers who want a durable hitch cord.
The 8 mm size suits many 11 to 13 mm climbing and rigging ropes, but hitch performance depends on both cord and host rope. Test it before relying on it. Browse our hitch cord for other sizes.
Thimble prusiks are also used on rigging lines as a tie-off or to hold the line when resetting a lowering device. Make sure the cord and thimbles are rated for the use you put them to.
Tie the hitch you have been trained on and set it low to test grip and release. Watch for glazing, heat damage and wear near the eyes.
Hitch cord used in a climbing system is life-support equipment. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspect it before every use and retire it at the first sign of damage.

faq.q: What rope sizes does it work on?
faq.a: Many climbers use 8 mm cord on 11 to 13 mm rope, but grip varies. Test on your rope before climbing or rigging.

faq.q: Can I use it in a climbing system?
faq.a: Only if the manufacturer rates it for life support. Check the listing and instructions before using it to climb.

name: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Type C Chainsaw Pants (Black)
title: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Type C Chainsaw Pants
h1: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Chainsaw Pants (Type C, Black)
meta: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro chainsaw pants with Type C protection for climbers and saw hands who want all-round leg coverage. Fit, care and how they compare.
tagline: Light, breathable chainsaw pants with all-round leg protection for climbers.
summary: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro chainsaw pants are lightweight, breathable saw pants with Type C protection, meaning the protective layers wrap around the leg rather than just the front. They are a common choice for climbers who run a top-handle saw aloft, where a cut can come from any angle.
highlights: Type C all-round leg protection
Breatheflex stretch fabric for climbing
Black color
Built for saw work in the tree and on the ground
Arbortec's top-tier Breatheflex Pro line

p: Most chainsaw pants protect the front of the leg, because that is where a ground operator usually gets cut. In the tree you are moving around the saw, so a cut can reach the back of the leg too. Type C pants put protective layers around the whole leg, which is why they are popular with climbers.

The Breatheflex Pro line uses stretch fabric to keep the pants comfortable while climbing and moving around. Check the labels on the pair you buy for the exact protection class and standards, and see our chainsaw pants for other options.

Black is a practical choice for daily wear since it hides sap, dirt and bar oil well. Many climbers pair saw pants with a stretch work shirt or the matching Breatheflex jackets for a full kit that moves well aloft.
Get a fit that lets you lift your knees fully without the protection shifting. Wash them as the label directs, since the wrong detergent or heat can damage the protective layer.

Retire chainsaw pants once the protective layer is cut, as the fibers that stop the chain are pulled out. Saw protection reduces injury but does not make you immune; use proper technique and training under ANSI Z133.

faq.q: What does Type C mean?
faq.a: It means the protective material covers the whole leg rather than only the front. It suits climbing, where cuts can come from any angle.

faq.q: Are they hot in summer?
faq.a: Any saw pant is warmer than regular work pants, but the Breatheflex Pro line is designed to be breathable and stretchy for active work.

name: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Realtree Camo Jacket (Brown)
title: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Realtree Camo Jacket
h1: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Realtree Camo Jacket (Brown)
meta: The Arbortec Breatheflex Pro jacket in brown Realtree camo is a stretchy work jacket for climbing and ground work in cool weather. Fit and care notes inside.
tagline: Stretch work jacket in brown Realtree camo for cool-weather climbing and ground work.
summary: The Arbortec Breatheflex Pro jacket is a stretchy, breathable work jacket from Arbortec's top Breatheflex line, here in brown Realtree camo. It is made for climbers and ground workers who need to move freely in cool weather without overheating.
highlights: Breatheflex Pro stretch fabric
Brown Realtree camo pattern
Moves with you while climbing
Breathable for hard work in cool weather
Pairs with Breatheflex chainsaw pants

p: Tree work is hard on jackets: you are reaching, climbing, dragging brush and sweating, then standing still while the ground crew rigs. The Breatheflex Pro jacket uses stretch fabric so it does not bind across the shoulders and lets heat out when you are working hard.
The brown camo version suits crews who prefer a low-key look. If you need to be seen near traffic or on a busy site, the orange version is the better pick. More options are in our jackets section.

It also works as a layer for the drive in and the cold start of the morning, then comes off once you are warm. Pair it with Breatheflex chainsaw pants for a matching kit, but keep in mind that only the pants offer saw protection.
Size it so you can raise your arms fully without the hem riding up, with room for a layer underneath. A jacket that is too loose can catch on branches and gear.
Wash as the label directs and avoid harsh detergents. Keep in mind this is a work jacket, not chainsaw protection. Wear proper saw protection and high-visibility clothing where the job calls for it.

faq.q: Is this jacket chainsaw protective?
faq.a: No. It is a work jacket. Wear chainsaw protective pants or chaps for saw work.

faq.q: Is there a high-vis version?
faq.a: Yes, the Breatheflex Pro camo jacket also comes in orange, which is more visible on the job.

title: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Camo Jacket in Orange
h1: Arbortec Breatheflex Pro Realtree Camo Jacket (Orange)
meta: The Arbortec Breatheflex Pro camo jacket in orange Realtree gives climbers a stretchy work jacket that stands out in the canopy. Fit, care and how it is used.
tagline: Orange Realtree camo stretch work jacket that stands out in the canopy.
summary: The Arbortec Breatheflex Pro camo jacket in orange Realtree is a stretchy, breathable work jacket that is easier to spot in the canopy than darker colors. It is a good fit for climbers who want freedom of movement and want the ground crew to see them.
highlights: Breatheflex Pro stretch fabric
Orange Realtree camo pattern
Easier for the ground crew to spot
Breathable for hard work in cool weather
Pairs with Breatheflex chainsaw pants

p: The ground crew needs to know where the climber is before they drop a piece, start the chipper or pull a line. A bright jacket helps, especially in leafy canopies and low light. The orange camo version gives you that visibility with a pattern that hides dirt better than solid color.
The Breatheflex Pro fabric stretches, so it does not bind when you reach for a limb, and it lets heat out during hard climbs. See our jackets and sweatshirts for more.

It makes sense off the tree as well. A groundie running the chipper or the rope is easier for the climber to see too, which helps when the climber is calling a piece down. Pair it with matching Breatheflex chainsaw pants for a kit that moves well.
Size it with room to layer underneath and so the sleeves and hem stay put when you reach overhead.
Wash as the label directs. This jacket is not certified high-visibility apparel and is not chainsaw protection, so wear compliant high-vis near traffic and proper saw protection for cutting.
Tuck or remove loose drawcords before climbing so they cannot snag on branches or catch in the saw.

faq.q: Is this a certified high-vis jacket?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Check the label; for roadside work, wear apparel that meets the required high-visibility standard.

faq.q: How does it compare to the brown version?
faq.a: Same jacket and fabric, different color. Orange is easier to spot in the canopy.

name: Courant Phoenix 8 mm Loop Prusik with Aluminum Ring
title: Courant Phoenix 8mm Loop Prusik with Ring
h1: Courant Phoenix 8 mm Loop Prusik with Aluminum Ring
meta: The Courant Phoenix loop prusik pairs 8mm hitch cord with an aluminum ring for a smooth-tending friction hitch. How it is used, fit to your rope and inspection.
tagline: Courant Phoenix 8 mm loop prusik with an aluminum ring for friction hitches.
summary: The Courant Phoenix loop prusik is a closed loop of 8 mm Phoenix hitch cord paired with an aluminum ring. The loop forms the friction hitch, and the ring gives a clean, smooth connection point to tend it.
highlights: Courant Phoenix 8 mm hitch cord
Closed loop design
Aluminum ring for a clean connection
Used for friction hitches and adjusters
Compact and easy to inspect

body.h: How the loop and ring work
p: A loop prusik is tied around the host rope to form a friction hitch, and the ring connects the hitch to your system. The ring gives a smooth surface for the cord to bear on and a tidy place to clip, which helps the hitch tend and release consistently.

Courant's Phoenix cord is built for friction hitches. At 8 mm it suits many common climbing and lanyard ropes, but hitch behavior depends on the host rope, so test it before use. Our hitch cord and split tails section has other options.

Climbers use this setup on lanyards as an adjuster and on climbing systems as part of a hitch. The ring keeps the hitch clear of the carabiner gate and makes it easier to tend with a pulley, which helps the cord last longer.
Set the hitch low and test grip and release before committing. Watch for glazing, heat damage and wear where the cord meets the ring.
Hitch cord in a climbing system is life-support equipment. Follow Courant's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspect it before every use, and retire it at the first sign of damage.
Keep a spare loop in the gear bag; hitch cord wears faster than rope and swapping it takes minutes.

faq.q: What is it used for?
faq.a: Commonly as a friction hitch on a lanyard or climbing system, or as a rope grab. Check the manufacturer's approved uses.

faq.q: Will it grip my rope?
faq.a: 8 mm cord grips many 11 to 13 mm ropes, but test it on your own rope close to the ground first.
